edges.description: The candidacidal defect predisposes to invasive candidiasis, but only a minority of MPO-deficient individuals develop it, usually with a second risk factor such as diabetes mellitus.

nodes.description: There is no disease-specific therapy and asymptomatic individuals need no treatment. Invasive Candida infections are treated with systemic antifungal agents; amphotericin B cured extensive candidal skull-base osteomyelitis in a child with MPO deficiency.

evidence.reference_title: Myeloperoxidase deficiency with extensive candidal osteomyelitis of the base of the skull.
evidence.snippet: The child was treated successfully with amphotericin B.

nodes.description: Invasive Candida esophagitis, part of disseminated candidiasis, was found at autopsy in a pre-eclamptic woman with MPO deficiency.

evidence.reference_title: Lethal candida sepsis associated with myeloperoxidase deficiency and pre-eclampsia.
evidence.snippet: Toxemia with disseminated intravascular coagulation (DIC) and acute renal failure had masked the symptoms of invasive candida esophagitis and disseminated candidiasis in both lungs.

nodes.description: MPO-deficient neutrophils show increased phagocytic activity and increased superoxide production (enhanced lucigenin chemiluminescence), which is thought to compensate for the missing MPO system and to explain why most affected individuals do not suffer severe bacterial infection.
nodes.id: Compensatory Enhancement of the Respiratory Burst

evidence.reference_title: Phagocytic activity and oxidative burst of granulocytes in persons with myeloperoxidase deficiency.
evidence.snippet: The lack of myeloperoxidase activity is compensated for by an increased phagocytic activity, an increased production of superoxide anion (lucigenin-chemiluminescence)

evidence.reference_title: Chronic granulomatous disease (CGD) and complete myeloperoxidase deficiency both yield strongly reduced dihydrorhodamine 123 test signals but can be easily discerned in routine testing for CGD.
evidence.snippet: Lucigenin-enhanced chemiluminescence (LCL) is increased in neutrophils from MPO-deficient patients, whereas neutrophils from patients with CGD show a decreased response.

evidence.reference_title: Myeloperoxidase deficiency.
evidence.snippet: In the absence of MPO, auxiliary mechanisms protect most MPO-deficient hosts from clinically significant sequelae

nodes.description: Mutant MPO precursors are glycosylated and acquire heme but are retained in the endoplasmic reticulum in prolonged association with calreticulin and calnexin, are not proteolytically processed to mature subunits, and are degraded by the proteasome through endoplasmic reticulum quality control. Neutrophils therefore carry a 90-kDa precursor but no mature enzyme.

biological_processes: ER-associated degradation of mutant MPO precursor

evidence.reference_title: A novel form of hereditary myeloperoxidase deficiency linked to endoplasmic reticulum/proteasome degradation.
evidence.snippet: it was neither proteolytically processed to mature MPO subunits nor secreted. After prolonged association with calreticulin and calnexin in the endoplasmic reticulum, MPOY173C was degraded.

evidence.reference_title: Hereditary myeloperoxidase deficiency due to a missense mutation of arginine 569 to tryptophan.
evidence.snippet: neutrophils from individuals with MPO deficiency lack enzymatic and immunochemical evidence for mature MPO but have a 90-kDa precursor protein

nodes.description: Candida meningitis has been reported, and in one child with compound heterozygous MPO deficiency it led to a mistaken diagnosis of chronic granulomatous disease because of a low dihydrorhodamine oxidation signal.

evidence.reference_title: Complete Myeloperoxidase Deficiency: Beware the "False-Positive" Dihydrorhodamine Oxidation.
evidence.snippet: A patient with Candida meningitis and low dihydrorhodamine oxidation signal was diagnosed with chronic granulomatous disease but actually had compound heterozygous myeloperoxidase deficiency.

nodes.description: Candida albicans liver abscess has been reported in a diabetic patient with hereditary MPO deficiency.

evidence.reference_title: Leukocyte myeloperoxidase deficiency and diabetes mellitus associated with Candida albicans liver abscess.
evidence.snippet: Reported here is a case of hereditary myeloperoxidase deficinecy in a diabetic patient suffering from a Candida albicans liver abscess.

nodes.description: Coexisting diabetes mellitus is the main clinical modifier. Hyperglycemia itself impairs the fungicidal activity of normal granulocytes, adding a second hit to the MPO-dependent candidacidal defect; most reported cases of serious Candida infection in MPO deficiency occurred in diabetic patients.

evidence.reference_title: Hereditary myeloperoxidase deficiency.
evidence.snippet: Fungicidal activity of normal granulocytes was shown to be impaired during the in vitro artificial hyperglycemic condition.

evidence.reference_title: Clinical manifestation of myeloperoxidase deficiency.
evidence.snippet: Infectious diseases, especially with species of Candida, have been observed predominantly in MPO-deficient patients who also have diabetes mellitus

evidence.reference_title: Myeloperoxidase deficiency.
evidence.snippet: except for some persons with diabetes mellitus who suffer severe candidal disease

nodes.description: Without MPO, hydrogen peroxide produced by the NADPH oxidase respiratory burst is not converted with chloride into hypochlorous acid and its downstream chlorinating oxidants inside the phagosome.

evidence.reference_title: Myeloperoxidase: friend and foe.
evidence.snippet: The initial product of the MPO-H2O2-chloride system is hypochlorous acid

evidence.reference_title: Myeloperoxidase: a target for new drug development?
evidence.snippet: A unique activity of MPO is its ability to use chloride as a cosubstrate with hydrogen peroxide to generate chlorinating oxidants such as hypochlorous acid, a potent antimicrobial agent.

evidence.reference_title: Phagocytic activity and oxidative burst of granulocytes in persons with myeloperoxidase deficiency.
evidence.snippet: This was demonstrated by comparing myeloperoxidase mass concentration measured with an enzyme immunoassay, lack of HOCl production

nodes.description: Killing of Candida albicans by MPO-deficient neutrophils is markedly impaired, while killing of Staphylococcus aureus is only minimally affected, so the clinical susceptibility that does occur is dominated by Candida.

evidence.reference_title: Myeloperoxidase deficiency: prevalence and clinical significance.
evidence.snippet: In assays of leukocyte function only minor defects in killing of Staphylococcus aureus by MPO-deficient cells were noted whereas killing of Candida albicans was much more impaired.

evidence.reference_title: Hereditary myeloperoxidase deficiency.
evidence.snippet: The microbicidal activity of the granulocytes was partially diminished with regard to Staphylococcus aureus and was almost nil with regard to Candida albicans.

evidence.reference_title: In vivo role of myeloperoxidase for the host defense.
evidence.snippet: MPO-KO mice showed severely reduced cytotoxicity to various microorganisms such as Candida albicans, Aspergillus fumigatus, and Klebsiella pneumoniae

nodes.description: Completely MPO-deficient neutrophils fail to form neutrophil extracellular traps, whereas partially deficient neutrophils form them; MPO acts cell-autonomously in NET formation.

evidence.reference_title: Myeloperoxidase is required for neutrophil extracellular trap formation: implications for innate immunity.
evidence.snippet: In contrast, neutrophils from partially MPO-deficient donors make NETs, and pharmacological inhibition of MPO only delays and reduces NET formation.

nodes.description: Peroxidase activity is absent (complete deficiency) or reduced (partial deficiency) in neutrophils and monocytes, while eosinophil peroxidase, encoded by a separate gene, is preserved.
nodes.id: Loss of Neutrophil and Monocyte Myeloperoxidase Activity

evidence.reference_title: Leukocyte myeloperoxidase deficiency and diabetes mellitus associated with Candida albicans liver abscess.
evidence.snippet: Peroxidase activity is completely absent from the neutrophils and monocytes although it is present in the eosinophils.

evidence.reference_title: Genetic characterization of myeloperoxidase deficiency in Italy.
evidence.snippet: Hereditary myeloperoxidase (MPO) deficiency (MPOD) is the most common neutrophil biochemical defect, and is characterized by a lack of peroxidase activity.

evidence.reference_title: Myeloperoxidase Deficiency.
evidence.snippet: is an autosomal recessive disorder caused by mutations in the MPO gene on chromosome 17

evidence.reference_title: A novel form of hereditary myeloperoxidase deficiency linked to endoplasmic reticulum/proteasome degradation.
evidence.snippet: We identified a novel missense mutation in the MPO gene at codon 173 whereby tyrosine is replaced with cysteine (Y173C) that is associated with MPO deficiency

nodes.description: Biallelic or compound heterozygous variants in MPO cause the disease. The most frequent allele in Western populations is the exon 10 missense variant R569W; other missense, frameshift, splice-site and small-deletion alleles (Y173C, M251T, the exon 9 14-base deletion, and several Italian and Japanese alleles) have been described. Several genotypes produce the same biochemical phenotype.

evidence.reference_title: Hereditary myeloperoxidase deficiency due to a missense mutation of arginine 569 to tryptophan.
evidence.snippet: At the amino acid level this mutation would replace arginine at codon 569 with tryptophan. Six of seven patients with complete MPO deficiency had this mutation.

evidence.reference_title: Genetic characterization of myeloperoxidase deficiency in Italy.
evidence.snippet: The genetic characterization of the subjects showed the presence of three already-known mutations (c.752T>C, c.1705C>T, and c.1566_1579del14) and six novel mutations

nodes.description: Absent (complete) or reduced (partial) neutrophil peroxidase activity, detected as an abnormal peroxidase index or displaced neutrophil cluster on peroxidase-based automated hematology analyzers and confirmed by cytochemistry. This is the defining laboratory feature.

evidence.reference_title: Prevalence of myeloperoxidase deficiency: population studies using Bayer-Technicon automated hematology.
evidence.snippet: Peroxidase deficiencies are manifested by the irregular location of these clusters. This makes it possible to identify persons totally or partially lacking myeloperoxidase.

evidence.reference_title: Myeloperoxidase deficiency: prevalence and clinical significance.
evidence.snippet: Partial (13 patients) or complete (13 patients) MPO deficiency was confirmed by examination of cytochemical stains in 26

nodes.description: Disseminated or visceral candidiasis is the characteristic serious complication, reported in fewer than 5% of MPO-deficient subjects and predominantly in those with diabetes mellitus; fatal Candida sepsis has been reported.

evidence.reference_title: Clinical manifestation of myeloperoxidase deficiency.
evidence.snippet: but the frequency of such cases is very low, less than 5% of reported MPO-deficient subjects

evidence.reference_title: Lethal candida sepsis associated with myeloperoxidase deficiency and pre-eclampsia.
evidence.snippet: Candida sepsis was discovered as the cause of death at postmortem examination. Myeloperoxidase (MPO) deficiency was identified as having supported the invasive candida infection.

nodes.description: Extensive Candida albicans osteomyelitis of the skull base and first cervical vertebra was reported in a child whose neutrophils lacked MPO.

evidence.reference_title: Myeloperoxidase deficiency with extensive candidal osteomyelitis of the base of the skull.
evidence.snippet: A CT scan of the mastoids showed extensive bone destruction of the base of the skull and C-1.

evidence.reference_title: Myeloperoxidase deficiency with extensive candidal osteomyelitis of the base of the skull.
evidence.snippet: histopathologic findings were suggestive of mycotic infection and cultures were positive for Candida albicans

nodes.description: Disseminated pustular candidal dermatitis was reported in a nondiabetic MPO deficient man receiving narrow-spectrum antibiotic therapy.

evidence.reference_title: Myeloperoxidase deficiency manifesting as pustular candidal dermatitis.
evidence.snippet: We present a case of myeloperoxidase deficiency manifesting as disseminated pustular candidal dermatitis in a nondiabetic male.
